edges.description: Loss of the RAB11 GAP leaves RAB11-dependent recycling unregulated.
TBC1D8B sits on maturing endosomes and is needed for cargo processing.
Nephrin is delivered to and recycled from the slit diaphragm through RAB11 endosomes.
Nephrin turnover depends on endocytosis through maturing endosomes.
Loss of correctly placed nephrin undermines the slit diaphragm and the podocyte foot processes.
Loss of the single zebrafish ortholog causes proteinuria, rescued by wild-type but not patient-mutant human mRNA.
edges.limitations: The larval zebrafish pronephros is a simplified glomerular filter, and FSGS-type lesions and progression to kidney failure cannot be assessed in this model.

edges.description: Nephrocyte-restricted mislocalization of the nephrin ortholog Sns.
edges.limitations: Nephrocytes form slit diaphragms but are not glomerular podocytes, and the fly has no glomerular filtration or proteinuria readout comparable to the human disease.

edges.description: Endosomal maturation and cargo degradation are disturbed in the null nephrocytes.
edges.limitations: Whether endosomal maturation is defective in human podocytes has not been tested.

nodes.description: In Drosophila nephrocytes a null Tbc1d8b allele disturbs endosomal maturation and degradation, and silencing the maturation regulator Hrs reproduces the defect. This step is shown only in the fly.

nodes.description: TBC1D8B binds nephrin, and its loss mislocalizes nephrin (Sns in Drosophila) away from the slit diaphragm. The human evidence is the nephrin interaction in cell lines; the mislocalization itself is shown in nephrocytes.
